clue.text: Release catch in more ways than one

definitions.text: Release catch in more ways than one

parts.words: Release catch in more ways than one
parts.note: to free a hooked fish is to release a catch, and to undo a fastening is to release a catch too, so the one verb fits both senses

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to free something from a hook and to unfasten a clasp or latch.

clue.text: Protection against feline and canine onslaught?

definitions.text: Protection against feline and canine onslaught?

parts.words: Protection against feline and canine onslaught?
parts.note: it is raining cats and dogs, so the shelter needed is against a heavy downpour

explanation.definitionFit: A canopy carried overhead keeps off heavy rain, the idiomatic cats and dogs.

clue.text: Noted producer of Mars bars?

parts.note: Mars is a planet and bars are measures of music, so this is the composer of the noted piece, not a chocolate maker

explanation.definitionFit: The English composer wrote The Planets, whose first movement is Mars, the Bringer of War.

clue.text: Step off liner and all may follow this cardinal

definitions.text: Step off liner and all may follow this cardinal

parts.words: Step off liner and all may follow this cardinal
parts.note: take liner away from a joke type called a something-liner, put and all after a word for a common phrase, and give the lowest cardinal number

explanation.definitionFit: It is the first cardinal number, and precedes both liner and and all in set phrases.

clue.text: Wife I left in drunken state of decline

indicators.note: the first three pieces are put in the word for drunken

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A husband walks out drunk and the marriage slides downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, the closing period of anything after its peak, as in the dusk of a career.

clue.text: Beating of wrath?

indicators.note: beating batters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Anger is expressed by a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating' both mixes up the letters of OF and WRATH and defines the answer: to give someone what for is to punish them.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone what for is to punish or scold them severely, a beating born of anger.

clue.text: Landlords retaining weight, eating minute slimline bangers?

indicators.note: the landlords hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: landlords let property, so they are letters

indicators.note: the weight swallows the abbreviation for minute

parts.note: a bob is the weight on a pendulum or plumb line

explanation.surface: Landlords keep their weight down by eating low-fat sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangers' looks like sausages (British slang) but means explosives; slimline because they fit in an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosive devices sent through the post are thin enough to pass as mail, hence slim bangers.

clue.text: Topping finally runs when ice melts — it's at zero degrees

indicators.note: only the closing letter of topping is used

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: melting breaks the letters down and reforms them

explanation.surface: When the ice melts, the topping runs off at last, at freezing point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero degrees' suggests freezing; it means longitude, Greenwich being on the prime meridian.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime meridian, longitude zero, passes through the London observatory there.

clue.text: Times hosting free service

indicators.note: the times letters contain the free word

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time, so two of them make times
to ease is to free or loosen

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper offers a complimentary service.
explanation.definitionFit: A service is a matching set of crockery, such as cups and saucers for tea.

clue.text: Hammer tack unevenly into canvas

indicators.note: to hammer is to batter, so the letters are knocked into a new shape
the odd-numbered letters of into are kept

explanation.surface: Someone hammers a tack crookedly into a canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: A kit-cat is a portrait canvas size, about 36 by 28 inches, named after the Kit-Cat Club's portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a standard size of canvas for portraits, used for the Kit-Cat Club's members.

clue.text: Parisian's to go inside ditch with a girl on point duty

indicators.note: the French verb sits within the word for ditch

parts.note: to bin something is to ditch it
aller is French, the language of Paris, for to go

explanation.surface: A Frenchman jumps into a ditch beside a girl directing traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point duty' suggests a traffic officer; here it means dancing on the points of the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet dancer works en pointe, on the tips of her toes, so she is a girl on point duty.

clue.text: Letter volunteers read out

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the phrase for the volunteers gives the letters of a Greek character

parts.note: ..., the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve; spoken as the plus the two letter names

explanation.surface: Volunteers have a letter read out to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army; 'the TA', read out as the letters are said, approximates the Greek letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Ready to go in

parts.note: ready is slang for cash (the readies), so this is the cash paid to be admitted

explanation.definitionFit: It is the money charged for admission, ready cash being the readies.

clue.text: Half the alphabet, I demonstrated, needs nothing added in for making very fine pieces

parts.note: A to M is the first half of the alphabet

indicators.note: nothing is placed inside the protest word

parts.note: to sit in is to demonstrate, so sat in
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shows how half the alphabet can be broken into tiny bits.
explanation.definitionFit: The process turns a liquid into a fine spray, reducing it to tiny particles.

clue.text: Originally called section of telephone exchange

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut out of the longer run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A part of the telephone exchange was once known by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a maiden name, it means born as, that is, originally called.

clue.text: Lake, perhaps, to become known

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says take four letters and arrange them out of order; one result is the word lake

explanation.surface: A lake might seep away and become public knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction (an anagram of a four-letter word for seep), can produce 'Lake', hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret information that escapes into public view is said to do this.

clue.text: Almost clear escape — heads of Allied prisoners withheld consent

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to acquit is to clear of a charge

indicators.note: the initials are kept back from the word escape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Allied prisoners, nearly cleared, are refused permission to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquiesce is to accept or agree without protest, that is to consent.

clue.text: Animal talk

explanation.definitionFit: It is the burrowing animal, and in British slang to rabbit on is to talk at length.

clue.text: One dropping charges was full of hot air

definitions.text: One dropping charges was full of hot air

parts.words: One dropping charges was full of hot air
parts.note: dropping charges means releasing bombs, not abandoning a lawsuit, and the craft was filled with gas

explanation.definitionFit: German airships bombed Britain in the First World War and were lifted by gas, here gas being hot air.

clue.text: In hollow economy, leave a union

indicators.note: the word for leave goes in the shell of economy
economy hollowed out keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: With the economy hollowed out, workers choose to leave their union.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of the trade union representing actors and performers in Britain.

clue.text: Barrel loony oddly knocked over, where soldiers may go for a dip

definitions.text: where soldiers may go for a dip

indicators.note: a barrel knocked over lies the other way, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: a cask is a barrel

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of loony are kept

explanation.surface: A mad soldier knocks over a barrel and goes for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are British strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk of an egg is where toast soldiers are dipped, so the yolk's membrane bag fits.

clue.text: Dick's plimsoll needing a slight alteration

indicators.note: a slight alteration is a change of one letter, here the second

parts.note: a plimsoll is a canvas gym shoe

explanation.surface: Someone's canvas sports shoe needs a minor repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick's' is 'Dick is', with 'dick' being slang for a detective; a plimsoll is a light canvas sports shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a private detective, from the soft-soled shoes that let him follow quietly.

clue.text: Injured rook looked outside

indicators.note: the looking word lies outside the chess letter

parts.note: gazed means looked steadily
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: An injured rook looked on from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A grazed limb has had its skin scraped, so it is injured slightly.

clue.text: Very good boxing points divided by team that's annoying

indicators.note: very good encloses the rest, as a box surrounds
the two points are split by the team

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Very good boxing judges' points are split by a team, which is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport; it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating or troublesome is annoying in just this way.

clue.text: Priest making regular appearances in the colonies

indicators.note: every third letter of the phrase the colonies is taken, a regular pattern

explanation.surface: A priest turns up from time to time in the colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who brought up Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical priest of Shiloh who raised the young prophet Samuel.

clue.text: Very efficient removal man apparently skiving on the job?

definitions.meaning: a thorough clear-out of everything, as in an election rout

definitions.text: man apparently skiving on the job?
definitions.meaning: a chimney cleaner who stays spotless seems not to have been working

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a complete clearing-out, and humorously a spotless chimney cleaner who must have avoided work.

clue.text: Entirely new navigation unit intended primarily to make one list less when connected

definitions.text: to make one list less when connected

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the five words are used

explanation.surface: A fresh navigation unit is supposed to shorten one list once wired up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List less' joined up reads listless: ennui is what makes one listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom and weariness are what leave a person listless, the two words run together.

clue.text: Go away from 27 area — I am taking transport without pressure

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: the pressure letter is removed from the vehicle word

parts.note: a ship is a means of transport
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A man tells someone to leave the canal zone while boarding a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Imshi was British forces' slang, from Arabic, for go away, picked up in Egypt around the Suez Canal (27).
explanation.definitionFit: It is army slang borrowed from Egyptian Arabic, an order to clear off heard in the canal zone.

clue.text: Girl caught by God from the East in narrow passage

annotationWithheld.why: 'Girl caught by God from the East in narrow passage' (4,5): reversed ZEUS gives SUEZ, and 'narrow passage' gives CANAL, but then 'Girl caught by' (SUE inside SUEZ) is description rather than wordplay and there is no separate definition; no clean parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: Girl caught by God from the East in narrow passage

clue.text: Group of workers reported in vineyard.

indicators.note: said aloud, the work team gives the French wine word

parts.note: a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: A team of workers is said to be in a vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: In French wine classification a cru is a vineyard or its graded growth.

clue.text: Grecian urn originally thrown as a piece of art

indicators.note: as a potter throws clay into shape, these letters are reshaped
only the opening letter of urn is used

explanation.surface: A Greek pot was thrown and became a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernica is Picasso's 1937 painting of the bombing of the Basque town.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso's famous large anti-war painting is a celebrated work of art.

clue.text: Judge gets to catch you, reportedly round a boy

indicators.note: said aloud, the pronoun gives a single letter

parts.note: the pronoun spoken sounds like the letter U

indicators.note: the catching verb is turned round

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A judge arrives to catch you, as it is reported, around a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a boy's given name.
